exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 1–6, consider a Markov chain with state space with $$\left\{ 1,2,\ldots,n \right\}$$ and the given transition matrix. Identify the communication classes for each Markov chain as recurrent or transient, and find the period of each communication class.

In Exercises 7–10, consider a simple random walk on the given directed graph. Identify the communication classes of this Markov chain as recurrent or transient, and find the period of each communication class.

problem.paragraph: Let $$A$$ be an $$n \times n$$ matrix and let $$E$$ be an $$n \times n$$ matrix resulting from permuting the rows of $$I_{n}$$ , the $$n \times n$$ identity matrix. The matrix $$E$$ is called a permutation matrix.

list.item: Show that $$EA$$ is the matrix $$A$$ with its rows permuted in exactly the same order that the rows of $$I_{n}$$ were permuted to form $$E$$ . Hint: Any permutation of rows can be written as a sequence of swaps of pairs of rows.
Apply the result of part (a) to $$A^{T}$$ to show that $$AE^{T}$$ is the matrix $$A$$ with its columns permuted in exactly the same order that the rows of $$I_{n}$$ were permuted to form $$E$$ .
Explain why $$EAE^{T}$$ is the matrix $$A$$ with its rows and columns permuted in exactly the same order that the rows of $$I_{n}$$ were permuted to form $$E$$ .
In the process of finding the canonical form of a transition matrix, does it matter whether the rows of the matrix or the columns of the matrix are permuted first? Why or why not?

problem.paragraph: First note that states $$1$$ and $$3$$ communicate with each other, as do states $$2$$ and $$4$$ . However, there is no way to proceed from either state $$1$$ or state $$3$$ to either state $$2$$ or state $$4$$ , so the communication classes are $$\left\{ 1 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ and $$\left\{ 2 \text{,} 4 \right\}$$ . Since the chain stays in class $$\left\{ 1 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ after it enters this class, class $$\left\{ 1 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ is recurrent. Likewise, there is a positive probability of leaving class $$\left\{ 2 \text{,} 4 \right\}$$ at any time, so class $$\left\{ 2 \text{,} 4 \right\}$$ is transient. One ordering of the states that produces a canonical form is $$1$$ , $$3$$ , $$2$$ , $$4$$ : the corresponding transition matrix is $$1 & 3 & 2 & 4 1 & 3 & 2 & 4 P \rightarrow_{ \text{columns} }^{ \text{rearrange} } \begin{bmatrix} 1 / 4 & 1 / 2 & 1 / 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 3 \\ 3 / 4 & 1 / 2 & 0 & 1 / 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 3 \end{bmatrix} 1 2 3 4 \rightarrow_{ \text{rows} }^{ \text{rearrange} } \begin{bmatrix} 1 / 4 & 1 / 2 & 1 / 3 & 0 \\ 3 / 4 & 1 / 2 & 0 & 1 / 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 3 \end{bmatrix} 1 3 2 4$$
